title: Set Me As a Seal
summary: This is the permanent sealing — coda, not new movement. Five teachings close the cycle. The first and longest stands at the heart of the coda: the prayer that arises when divine humanity is in great affliction, the petition raised on its behalf, the operative power sent in answer, the discrimination accomplished, the conjunction made permanent — the entire cycle remembered and gathered into one structural prayer. The next distinguishes what is pruned without pain from what is cut at real cost — the soul learning the difference between surface and structural, what the seal binds and what falls away of itself. Then the inner sight opening in those whose body's eye blossoms — the eye now seeing what before was hidden. Then the two essences finally and forever distinguished: what is given, what is claimed, the beautiful separated forth from the darkness. The corpus closes with the structural supports of the regenerated rational and the identification of the Yes and the Amen: the Calling and the Hearing become the soul's permanent answering — what reigns over the whole work, refines the Living Soul, and grants her remembrance.
organizing_principle: The five teachings perform the sealing. The first and longest of the coda does at the soul-level what an earlier teaching did at the macro-cosmic level — narrates the entire redemptive descent and ascent — but now as the prayer that bears it: the cry from affliction, the petition, the answering powers sent, the conjunction sealed. This is the seal set upon the heart. The next is the seal set upon the working life — the discrimination of what is pruned without pain (surface outgrowth) from what is cut at real cost (structural member); the soul has learned which loosenings are which, and the seal holds what should hold, releases what should release. Then the eye that blossoms — the inner sight permanently opened, the rational loosed in stillness from the natural's claim, the seeing that does not pass. Then the foundational distinction set forever: two essences, what is given and what is claimed, the beautiful separated from the darkness — what is now distinguished cannot be mingled again. The corpus closes with the Yes and the Amen: the Calling and the Hearing identified as the soul's answering, that which reigns through the whole work and is itself the refiner, helper, and rememberer of the Living Soul. Two of these chapters survive in damaged condition, but the surviving threads carry the doctrinal close. The seal is set; the cycle is complete.
